name: Pop Art (web)
summary: Flat, saturated colour, thick outlines, halftone dots and repeated mass-media images. It came from Britain and the USA in the 1950s and 1960s and treats advertising and comics as high art.

philosophy.core_thesis: Mass culture is the subject: the comic, the ad and the label become art when you make them big, flat and loud.
design_principles: Use 4 saturated colours at most on a page (red, yellow, blue and one of pink or cyan) and black outlines of 3px to 5px.
Make halftone dots with a 6px to 10px pitch at 100% opacity as a fill for backgrounds and shadows.
Repeat an image 2 to 4 times in a grid, each copy in a different colour set.
Set headlines in a heavy comic or poster face at 56px or larger with a 3px black outline or a hard 4px offset shadow.
Place speech bubbles and burst shapes (8 to 16 points) around calls to action.
Crop photographs hard and reduce them to 3 to 4 flat colours.
Keep copy short: headlines of 1 to 6 words and slogans in capitals.
anti_patterns: Photographic realism without flat colour reduction
Quiet, minimal layouts with large empty areas
Serif body text set at display size

layout.grid_mechanics: A loose 12-column grid that allows repeated tiles of equal size; panel frames of 3px to 5px follow a comic page.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 10% to 20% of the surface stays empty; the spacing scale is 8, 16, 24 and 48px.
layout.alignment_rules: Centred or flush left; speech bubbles and bursts break the column; type may tilt by 1° to 3°.
layout.container_geometry: Rectangles with a 0px to 8px radius and a 3px to 5px black outline; bursts and bubbles with tails.

font_pairings.note: A fat poster face with a friendly comic text face.
A rounded single-family setting that can be pushed to heavy weights.

typography.tracking: Display takes 0.01em; body stays at 0; labels take +0.04em.
hierarchy_rules: Use two weights for body: regular (400) and bold (700); display has one weight.
Set headlines in upper case with an outline.
Put a numeral or an exclamation mark in a burst shape next to a key claim.

color.palette_structure: Flat primaries and one hot pink on cream or white, outlined in black.
color.contrast_rules: Black on yellow holds 14:1; white on red holds at least 4.5:1 for bold text of 24px and larger.
color.surface_treatment: Flat opaque inks with halftone dot fills; no gradients.
color.light_and_shadow: No light source; hard 4px offset shadows in black.

materiality.surface_simulation: Cheap four-colour print: flat inks and visible halftone dots.
materiality.border_rules: Solid black outline of 3px to 5px on every container and image.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: No blur. Hard offset shadow of 4px 4px 0 black on cards and buttons.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Solid icons with a heavy 3px outline in black, round joins and a flat colour fill; place each in a burst or a circle.
ornamentation_details.illustration: Comic panels, speech bubbles and repeated, colour-shifted portraits or products.

motion.transition_physics: Translation for screen: quick, snappy pops with a small overshoot; elements stamp in at a scale of 1.08, then settle at 1.0.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover moves the card by 2px and cuts the offset shadow to 2px; active state removes the shadow.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels a loud, ironic fun, as in a comic book or an advert.

avoid_when: The product is serious, medical or financial.
The page needs calm long reading.
The brand is premium and quiet.

modifiers.how: Mute the palette to earth tones and drop the outlines and dots; keep the flat shapes.
Keep the outline and offset shadow; drop the halftone and the bursts.
Add squiggles and confetti patterns and rotate elements by up to 3°.

pack.why: A bold outline with a flat fill that looks like a comic panel.

ground.why: Pop art enlarges the Ben-Day dots of comic print until the dots become the picture.
